photo_prompt: Mach dieses foto kolorisiert und als wäre es mit einem handy aufgenommen wurde. Bewahre Identität, Gesicht, Frisur, Kleidung und Pose. Natürliche Farben und echte Hauttextur, klare Smartphone-Fotoqualität. Einzelnes vertikales Kopf-und-Schulter-Porträt, Kopf vollständig sichtbar, ohne Text oder andere Personen.

parties.name: National Democratic Party
parties.historical_note: Founded historically in 1978. Anwar Sadat, vice-president in January 1970, is its prospective founder in this alternate path.

parties.name: Conservative Party
parties.historical_note: The later Conservative Party is retained. Retired vice-president Zakaria Mohieddin is an alternate founding candidate for a conservative, pro-Western platform.

parties.name: Free Egyptians Party
parties.historical_note: Founded historically in 2011. Entrepreneur Osman Ahmed Osman represents an alternate early foundation; this is not a claim of historical party membership.

parties.name: Egyptian Social Democratic Party
parties.historical_note: Founded historically in 2011. Ibrahim Shukri is an alternate 1970 candidate for parliamentary social reform, not its historical founder.

parties.name: Egyptian Communist Party
parties.historical_note: The communist organisations dissolved themselves in 1965; a party revival is an alternate path. Free Officer and former HADITU associate Khaled Mohieddin is an alternate leadership candidate, not a historical ECP chairman in January 1970.

parties.name: Revolutionary Socialists
parties.historical_note: The later Revolutionary Socialists are retained. Exiled communist Henri Curiel is an alternate candidate for an independent revolutionary left; he was not a historical leader of this later Trotskyist organisation.

parties.name: Dignity Party (Karama)
parties.historical_note: The later Karama party is retained. Free Officer Hussein el-Shafei represents an alternate early Nasserist foundation.

parties.name: Arab Democratic Nasserist Party
parties.historical_note: The later Nasserist party is retained. Ali Sabri, a senior ASU politician in 1970, leads its alternate early incarnation.

parties.name: Shi'a Reform Party
parties.historical_note: A fictional Egyptian Shi'a reform party. No organised Egyptian party or personal leader of this doctrine is attested for January 1970; a collective council is used.

parties.name: Islamic Guardianship Party
parties.historical_note: A fictional Egyptian party of Islamic jurists. An Iranian-style Egyptian theocracy is an alternate-history option, represented by a collective council.

parties.name: Al-Nour Party
parties.historical_note: Founded historically in 2011. Egyptian Salafi scholar Abd al-Razzaq Afifi, then resident in Saudi Arabia, is an alternate founding candidate, not a historical Al-Nour chairman.

parties.name: Ansar Bayt al-Maqdis
parties.historical_note: The later organisation is retained as an alternate-history faction. Its modern commanders were not active adult leaders in 1970; a collective leadership is used.

parties.name: Muslim Brotherhood
parties.historical_note: Hassan al-Hudaybi was General Guide from 1951 until 1973. The organisation is banned at the start; a government takeover requires an alternate political path.

parties.name: Coptic Orthodox Church
parties.historical_note: Pope Cyril VI headed the Church from 1959 to 1971. The Church is represented as a political faction for gameplay, not a historical electoral party.

parties.name: New Wafd Party
parties.historical_note: Founded historically in 1978 as the revival of the Wafd dissolved in 1953. Veteran Fouad Serageddin is the prospective founder.

parties.name: Republican People's Party
parties.historical_note: The later party is retained. Entrepreneur Osman Ahmed Osman is an alternate 1970 candidate for its business-oriented programme, not its historical founder.

parties.name: Reform and Development Party
parties.historical_note: The later party is retained. Finance minister Abdel Aziz Hegazy is an alternate founding candidate for economic and administrative reform.

parties.name: Egyptian Green Party
parties.historical_note: Founded historically in 1990. Geologist Rushdi Said, head of the mining and geological research organisation in 1970, is an alternate environmentalist candidate.

parties.name: Arab Socialist Union
parties.historical_note: The sole legal political organisation in January 1970. Gamal Abdel Nasser remains president; Anwar Sadat is the default successor after his death.

parties.name: National Progressive Unionist Rally Party (Tagammu)
parties.historical_note: Founded historically in 1976. Free Officer Khaled Mohieddin is its prospective founder and an independent socialist candidate in 1970.

parties.name: Homeland Defenders Party
parties.historical_note: The later party is retained. Free Officer Kamal el-Din Hussein is an alternate early nationalist candidate, not its historical chairman.

parties.name: Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party - Egypt Region
parties.historical_note: The later Egyptian Ba'ath organisation is retained as a playable party. A regional leadership council avoids assigning an unrelated Egyptian politician to this movement.

parties.name: Egyptian Armed Forces
parties.historical_note: War minister and commander-in-chief Mohamed Fawzi represents direct military rule. In January 1970 he serves under Nasser, rather than heading a separate ruling party.

parties.name: Muhammad Ali Dynasty
parties.historical_note: Fuad II lives in exile and is seventeen on 1 January 1970, turning eighteen on 16 January. Restoration is an alternate-history route.
